[Spoiler text](/spoiler) which turns into Spoiler text

[text](/s "Spoiler text") which turns into text

Another difference between the Netherlands and say the US is that they have their own bike lanes meaning that the chance of hitting a car is a lot lower.
I just visited Amsterdam and took a bike tour there. I was amazed by how well all the different forms of traffic worked with each other. I wish large cities in the US were built around bikes.

This is what REAL bicycle traffic looks like once you get past the novelty phase. No spandex, no helmets, no high-tech components. Just regular people, using basic bikes as a transportation device - because it makes sense, at least in metropolitan areas. By the way - did you notice how many people wear business outfits? You really believe all of them are going to take a shower once they arrive at their offices? No, they won't. Because they don't need to. You are not going to sweat if you just cruise at a normal speed (and do it every day). So there goes your excuse against using a bike for your commute.

What do you think of No Mans Sky?
What are your impressions on No Mans Sky?
Look's like fun, but like Smook_LV, Vouch it might not be satisfying after much time invested. I really like the exploration, generated world. Fantastic idea.
Looks a bit boring to be honest. If you want a space combat sim elite dangerous seems like a better option.

When I first saw it, the concept blew me away but every video that comes out for it now looks the same. Fly a ship, land on a random planet, see some animals, then hop back in the ship and fly away and maybe get into a space battle in between. That seems like it'll be cool for a bit but i think it'll get pretty repetitive fast. I really want it to be good but i'm kind of over games about exploring random empty worlds. I did that in minecraft, terraria, and starbound already, and in those there were dungeons, cave systems, villages, etc. It doesn't seem like the planets in No Mans Sky are going to have any of this so what am i going to do there? I was super hyped before, but i think its kinda worn off and they haven't shown anything to recapture my interest unless i've missed something?

The size of the world and the way it is generated makes me think about Daggerfall (which is never a bad thing). The game itself is only a bonus for me anyway- I'm more excited about the 65daysofstatic soundtrack. I love that band!

I am not sure about it all, I loved spore and this seems (like @SmooK_LV said) this is in the same vein, but it grabbed one thing I hated about spore, it's a bit to cute and cartoony for my liking. Now if they were open to modding or getting into a darker side of space and exploration that would help out, but I feel they are very suck on the eutectic they have now.

That said I think I will play it if it come out and preforms reasonably on PC. I love all the space sims coming out and each does one more thing or refines the play just a bit more. Good times to own a PC.

A very impressive game, but I am worried that it might be too one sided and become repetitive over time.

However I am going to play it and see how it plays and make my own judgment of it.

It is impressive. What is bothering me is that even though most of the planets were never visited before, they all magically have beacons and sentinels. I get that this is a mechanic to prevent griefers to start destroying every planet they find, but still it's a bit weird.

I'm hoping that there's more variety like gassy planets, planets with no life at all, very dangerous but filled with expensive minerals to be mined. Planets with very hostile inhabitants and things like that.

It seems that life is too common. There are even aliens living on moons everywhere. But again, maybe it's like this so the game doesn't get boring too fast.

Really love the graphics, it's got a fairly unique art style. I've seen a lot of people say they're worried about repetitive gameplay and while I share that feeling somewhat, I think it looks varied enough and also visually impressive enough to hopefully detract from any tedious gameplay. But the combat looks really basic that needs some work imo.

I think the idea is really awesome and the realization too. I surely want to play it but probably I will not continue for long. I do not have so much time for gaming anymore and I that time I usually prefer a good single player story driven game. Still I might buy the game also to support this bold projects by indie studios!
Looks like a lot of space without much in it. I think the big challenge for the team will be creating enough content to keep the game interesting.

I think it'll fit in as a sort of zen garden. You don't play it to accomplish anything, or do anything in particular. You just come home from a bad day, hop in your ship, point yourself at a star, any star, and just go see what surprise lies beyond. It may not even surprise you, but then wouldn't that be a surprise as well?

This game isn't going to change gaming, and it's likely it won't live up to its hype. However, it will be there for a good few of us who just want to escape to another solar system.

I have been following this game for a while. And while I'm still excited. I am disappointed that its not a game where a friend and I can fly around together and explore. I also agree with other comments that the planets may have to little differences to hold interest. I feel like there is a lot about the game we don't know about yet though so I still have hope that it will be great!
Looks like it'll be fun for a month and then become boring but hopefully I'll be eating my words.

At this point - after watching the 18-minute gameplay - it seems to be still living in its glorified tech demo stages. The scale is impressive and I like the art style but I'm still not sure where the "game" is unless it's aiming to be one of those casual, roaming types of space sims (Drifter comes to mind; not super action packed but can be relaxing).
I was super excited about it, until Elite Dangerous caught my eye. Now I want it to be that game but know full well it won't. I am still think it could be captivating but will not hold my breath.
